newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing files McDonnell deal for EU approval.
newsitem.headline: Boeing files McDonnell deal for EU approval.

text.p: U.S. aircraft giant Boeing Co has formally requested the European Commission to clear its proposed acquisition of rival McDonnell Douglas Corp also of the United States, a Commission official told Reuters on Thursday.

The Commission, which must vet all large mergers and acquisitions which affect the European Union's market, has now about a month to decide whether to clear the deal or, as is more likely, to start an in-depth probe if it is worried about the impact on fair competition.

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert made it clear in December, when the $13.3 billion merger was announced, that conditions could be attached to the deal if it appeared that it would strengthen Boeing's already strong position in Europe.

A notice will be published in the EU's Official Journal shortly saying when the request was filed with the Commission -- which is when the preliminary one-month review starts ticking -- and seeking comments from interested parties.
The Commission official said the deal was notified early this week.

The European Airbus Industrie consortium, the only other serious competitor left in the aerospace industry, and its powerful partner companies are expected to file objections about the deal although their initial reaction reflected little concern.

Anthony Parr, European Director of British Aerospace, one of Airbus's partners, told Reuters in late December that the Boeing move could have trade implications besides the widely expected competition aspects.
Although he declined to elaborate, this was seen as potentially reigniting a dispute between the United States and Europe over subsidies paid to the industry on the two sides of the Atlantic.
Airbus's other partners are Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Aerospatiale of France and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas.

The Commission has the power to examine all corporate acquisitions or alliances involving companies with a combined worldwide turnover of five billion European currency units ($5.74 billion) and a European turnover of 250 millions ecus ($287 million) each.

It has blocked seven deals since 1991, including the planned merger of the platinum interests of South African company Gencor Ltd and Britain's Lonrho Plc. But it imposed conditions, such as asset divestment, on many others. $1 = 0.87 ecus
